title: A Mystery Text Adventure
author: tinselman
selftext:
Please give me feedback on this text adventure. It's inspired by early text adventures, like Zork.

It requires an anthropic key. Instructions are included.

[Play Mystery of the Burnt Elf](https://tinselman.github.io/BurntElf/)

comments.author: Felfedezni
comments.body: Would it be possible to allow the use of chatgpt oauth?

replies.author: tinselman
replies.body: No, sorry, I built it for Anthropic.

comments.author: dbraun31
comments.body: I'd be happy to give it a try. Do you have a recommendation as to how much to spend on "usage credits" for the Anthropic key in order to play? Also, do you prefer feedback dropped here, or is there a form in the game to give feedback, or drop feedback elsewhere?

replies.author: tinselman
replies.body: Feedback here is good. And it cost pennies.

replies.author: dbraun31
replies.body: This was so fun! It was definitely the most immersive in-game character interactions I've ever experienced. My full reaction and the whole game transcript can be found [here](https://gist.github.com/dbraun31/60e1a2259c6e9b56141ceeb0c0b44f4c) (let me know if you can't access for some reason).

replies.author: tinselman
replies.body:
A warning... it will work much better with better AI models. Fable isn't necessary. But Opus 4.8 works well.

Also, this is a total experiment. I wanted to see if I could create an interactive fiction with halfway believable characters. I did it here with text. But it may display where we'll eventually be headed with interactive characters in games. No more cut scenes. We will speak to characters. They will respond and interact.

replies.author: dbraun31
replies.body: Yea I totally get that vision. Very exciting potential for deeper immersion. I'll give it a shot and drop feedback here!
